scope: Three authenticated adaptive MediaMTX 1.21.1 trials on Linux ARM64 Docker with a 1500 kbit/s upstream capacity phase, public 3s automatic format down-hold and conservative visible-startup measurement. A separate 250ms Linux boot-time sampler observes host scheduling without changing media or acceptance thresholds.
boundaries: All three startup measurements, automatic format ladders and source-target recoveries pass, with six valid native boundaries and zero steady capacity/recovery freeze increments. Trials one and three pass all 23 gates.

Trial two fails playback because baseline frozen time increases by 207ms at 19:59:52.916 UTC, before impairment. The browser records a 199.9ms callback gap and a 109ms timer delay. Adjacent media receive times are 30.1ms apart while expected composition is 183.4ms apart; this event includes receiver-side presentation delay.

An independent 250ms Linux host sampler records a 330ms interval in the same window. This coincides with previous ten-minute host scheduling observations but does not prove their cause, fully explain the 207ms freeze, or retrospectively explain the separate 231ms event.

The complete series remains failed. Independent Linux MediaMTX qualification is the next discriminator; no production timing, buffering, congestion or continuity budget is relaxed. Measurements do not qualify physical capture/display, real OAuth, TURN or target hardware.
